forces.title: AI-Driven Digital Transformation Reshaping Real Estate Practices
forces.description: The Indian real estate sector is undergoing significant digital transformation, with AI adoption reaching 91% in corporate real estate by 2025. The increasing integration of Building Information Modeling (BIM), digital twins, IoT-enabled site monitoring, and AI-driven procurement optimization is fundamentally reshaping how construction projects are planned, executed, and managed. This shift creates new demand for advanced, integrated, and smart building components and systems.

forces.title: Incentives Driving Green and Sustainable Construction Practices
forces.description: The National Real Estate Policy 2025 includes incentives for green-certified developments, offering tax benefits and subsidies to promote sustainable construction practices. This policy shift is a major structural change that will increasingly drive demand for eco-friendly, energy-efficient, and sustainably sourced building products and systems, creating significant opportunities for manufacturers who adapt to these new standards.

forces.title: Industrialized Delivery Demands Advanced Supplier Capabilities
forces.description: Successful megaprojects, such as nuclear power plants, increasingly adopt an 'industrialized delivery' approach. This emphasizes securing long-lead components early, qualifying vendors to stringent nuclear standards, and providing multiyear demand visibility. For building product manufacturers, this signifies a structural shift towards requiring higher quality, advanced standardization, and predictable delivery capabilities to participate in large-scale, complex construction supply chains.

forces.title: Structural Inefficiencies and Overruns Impact Real Estate Projects
forces.description: Real estate projects in India are structurally exposed to inefficiencies, with 66% experiencing schedule overruns and 39% facing cost overruns. These issues are driven by fragmentation, rework, interdependencies across stakeholders, supply chain volatility, material cost inflation, lead-time unpredictability, and limited standardization in project delivery. This creates an unpredictable environment for building product manufacturers, affecting demand stability, project scheduling, and revenue forecasts.

forces.title: Massive Government Capital Outlay for Infrastructure Development
forces.description: The Union Budget 2026–27 increased the capital investment outlay for infrastructure to a record Rs. 12.22 lakh crore (US$ 132.8 billion), an 11.5% increase over the previous year. This substantial public spending on critical sectors like roads, railways, logistics, and urban infrastructure provides a guaranteed and continuous demand stream for building product manufacturers, underpinning strong market growth.

forces.title: Persistent Barriers to Digital Adoption in Real Estate
forces.description: Despite rapid AI adoption in certain segments, significant barriers persist in the Indian real estate sector, including fragmented systems, workforce skill gaps, high upfront costs, and organizational resistance to change. These factors can hinder the widespread implementation of advanced construction technologies and the adoption of corresponding innovative, digitally-integrated building products, potentially limiting market penetration for manufacturers offering such solutions.

forces.title: Robust Demand from Housing and Infrastructure Construction
forces.description: India's cement demand, which serves as a strong proxy for overall construction activity, is projected to grow at a 7-8% CAGR until FY27. This growth is sustained by the government's continued focus on urban and rural housing schemes and a robust pipeline of infrastructure projects. This healthy underlying demand directly translates into increased orders and sales opportunities for building product manufacturers, ensuring a stable market outlook.

forces.title: Streamlined Real Estate Project Approvals Boosting Efficiency
forces.description: The National Real Estate Policy 2025 has introduced a unified single-window clearance system for real estate projects, with the goal of streamlining approvals and reducing project delays by up to 40%. This regulatory improvement is a significant upside driver, as it promises faster project execution and a more consistent, predictable demand flow for building product manufacturers.

forces.title: Strong Momentum in Road and Highway Construction Projects
forces.description: India's national highways network expanded significantly to 1,46,342 km in FY25, with an expected addition of up to 13,000 km in 2025. The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways received an increased allocation of Rs. 3,09,875 crore (US$ 34.4 billion) in Budget FY27, and ambitious plans aim for a 2 lakh km national highway network by 2025. This ensures substantial and consistent demand for building products used in road infrastructure.

forces.title: Growing Private and Institutional Investment in Real Estate
forces.description: Institutional investments in India's real estate sector soared to US$ 10.50 billion in 2025, marked by a 52% surge in domestic capital contribution and sustained demand in office and residential segments. Private equity and venture capital investments also demonstrated significant growth and faster capital deployment cycles. This increased investor confidence and capital inflow directly fuels new real estate projects, expanding the overall market for building product manufacturers.

forces.title: Rising Demand for Green Steel in Construction Sector
forces.description: India's demand for green steel is projected to grow significantly, reaching 4.49 million tonnes by FY30, primarily driven by the construction sector. This shift indicates an increasing preference for sustainable raw materials within construction projects, which will influence the material composition, manufacturing processes, and sourcing strategies for building product manufacturers to meet evolving environmental standards and customer preferences.

forces.title: Digital Infrastructure Boom Driving Construction Demand
forces.description: Australia's data centre capacity is projected to more than double by 2030, driven by accelerating AI and cloud services demand. This expansion translates into significant construction activity, with an estimated US$100-120 billion in onshore economic impact from capital investment between 2026 and 2030. This robust growth in digital infrastructure construction directly fuels demand for specialized building products, components, and systems required for these advanced facilities.

viewpoints.title: Digital Transformation Redefining Indian Real Estate, Adoption Barriers Persist
viewpoints.description: KPMG foresees a fundamental rethinking of real estate operations in India, driven by technology adoption. While AI adoption in India's corporate real estate sector surged to 91% in 2025, fragmentation, workforce skill gaps, high upfront costs, and organizational resistance continue to present significant barriers to full-scale implementation. The increasing use of BIM, digital twins, IoT, and AI-driven analytics will shape future demand for building products, despite these persistent challenges in widespread adoption.

demand_drivers.description: India's urban population is estimated to reach 675.5 million by 2035 and 900 million by 2047, driving substantial demand for new housing, commercial spaces, and urban infrastructure, directly translating to increased building product requirements.

The residential sector is expected to deliver 10 million new homes in 2025-26, supported by record residential sales and strong demand for premium homes, fueling significant need for building materials and components.

demand_drivers.driver: Commercial and Retail Real Estate Expansion
demand_drivers.description: India's commercial real estate market is projected to grow at a 19.8% CAGR to US$ 253 billion by 2033, driven by high gross leasing activity and strong retail sector expansion, increasing demand for fit-outs and new construction building products.

India's hospitality sector is expected to add approximately 15,000-16,000 premium branded rooms, with occupancies set to rise, boosting demand for various building products for new constructions and renovations.

The PMAY-U 2.0 ‘Housing for All’ Mission, effective September 2024, aims to support one crore additional eligible beneficiaries over five years, directly stimulating housing construction and increasing demand for associated building products.

market_sizing.methodology: Real estate market valuation (2025, 2030) and projected market size (2047) are used as proxies for the underlying demand for building products in residential, commercial, retail, and hospitality construction across India. Rapid urbanization and government housing schemes are identified as key drivers for this demand.
